svg.title: Choose a runner according to the work a job does: Generate a self-hosted project with separate runners for checks and Docker
svg.text: Choose a runner according to the work a job does
Scenario: Generate a self-hosted project with separate runners for checks and Docker
Run the checks on real runners
Keep the project settings through an update

g.text: Given I generate a self-hosted project using the saas-linux-medium-amd64 Docker runner tag
and push it to GitLab
GitLab's page for .config/gitlab/ci/tags.yml on the main branch of the generated project. The file keeps the runner tag
given to Copier, ["saas-linux-medium-amd64"], and its comment says who uses it: "Runner selection for Docker jobs.
Native checks use .native-job instead."
The project's random name shows as "project". Its only commit is "chore: initial render".
When I open a merge request that adds the web application, its own lint settings and two
deliberate mistakes
The merge request's Changes tab. The file tree lists the 11 files it adds or changes, and .gitlab-ci.yml is not one of
them: the web application runs on the generated pipeline as it is.
The web application's plumbing is folded to its file names. The open diffs give the project dictionary
.config/cspell/config.project.json its own word, "hybridciword", and add the project's own lint settings in
project/quality/megalinter.yml. project/code/transport.js holds the first deliberate mistake, an http URL.
project/README.md holds the second, the misspelled word "spellling".
When the project gets an unprivileged runner for file checks and a Docker runner for
containers
Settings, CI/CD, Runners, once the merge request pipeline has run. The project has two runners of its own: "Docker jobs"
with the saas-linux-medium-amd64 tag, and "Unprivileged file checks" with no tag. The job counters read 9 for "Docker
jobs" and 8 for "Unprivileged file checks": 17 of the pipeline's 18 jobs ran, and code:all, the 18th, was skipped.
Then MegaLinter starts directly in its own image on the unprivileged runner
The code:megalinter job of that pipeline. Its open section, "Preparing the "docker" executor", says "Using Docker
executor with image ghcr.io/oxsecurity/megalinter": the check runs straight in MegaLinter's image, and no Docker service
starts. The side panel names the runner: Unprivileged file checks.
Under "Related jobs", code:megalinter is the only red one. Commitlint and the other file checks passed, and code:all,
which waits for them all, was skipped.
And MegaLinter rejects the misspelled word and the insecure URL and keeps its reports
The same job further down its log, with two MegaLinter sections open. devskim reports "warning: Insecure URL" at
project/code/transport.js:1:18. cspell reports "Unknown word (spellling)" in project/README.md, and does not flag
"hybridciword", the project's own word.
The job failed, and its side panel still offers the reports under "Job artifacts".
And code:all does not claim the checks passed while MegaLinter is red
GitLab's page for code:all in the same pipeline, the job that waits for every code check and then prints "All code
checks passed." MegaLinter failed, so GitLab never started it: "This job has been skipped".
Under "Related jobs", code:megalinter is red and code:all shows GitLab's grey skipped icon. A job whose only message is
"All code checks passed." no longer goes green while one of those checks is red.
When I update the project through Copier and correct both mistakes in the same merge request
GitLab's Compare revisions page, from the commit the merge request opened with to the branch after the next push. That
push brought two commits: "chore: update the toolbox through Copier" and "fix: correct spelling and use HTTPS".
Only four files changed. In .copier-answers.yml, _commit moves from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1, and the toolbox's own
.config/jq/Taskfile.yml gains the line "# e2e-update-marker". The README and transport.js carry the two fixes. The
runner tag, the project dictionary and the lint settings are not in the list: Copier kept them.
Then MegaLinter passes on the unprivileged runner and accepts both corrections
The code:megalinter job of the new pipeline, seen from the same place in its log. devskim and cspell now pass, with the
project's own word "hybridciword" still in the README, as the compare page above shows: the project dictionary came
through the update. The reports are kept again under "Job artifacts", and the runner is still Unprivileged file checks.
And code:all now reports that every code check passed
The same code:all page in the new pipeline. Every code check passed, so GitLab ran code:all this time: its log prints
"All code checks passed." and GitLab marks the job Passed. Under "Related jobs", every code check is green,
code:megalinter included.
And the Docker runner builds and tests the web application
The test job of the same pipeline. Its side panel says "Runner: Docker jobs" and "Tags: saas-linux-medium-amd64". Its
log starts the web application with Docker Compose, checks it and prints "PASS: the Compose web application returns the
expected HTTP response".

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 10 steps · 10 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
